Thailand and Cambodia have high chances to returning to an all out war as both sides contest a border drawn 100-years ago.

Cambodia currently hosting the 20th La Francophonie Summit put it’s neighbour on tentahook fearing Phnom Penh was going to introduce to delegates the fragile border dispute.

Prime Minister of Cambodia Hun Manet did not disappoint, he went ahead and splashed details of the dispute to an audience of over 90 heads of state and government gathered to discuss Francophonie matters.

During the opening ceremony of the Francophonie Summit today (15), the Cambodian leader alleged that Thailand remains in occupation of territory claimed by Cambodia.

Manet has described the situation along the disputed border as fragile.

However the two sides struck a ceasefire temporary ceasefire last December.

Manet noted that two rounds of armed conflict had resulted in casualties and forced 20000 people to flee.

“Approximately 20,000 Cambodians are still unable to return to their homes.” “Ensuring their safe and dignified return remains our top priority,” Manet said.

The Premeir told delegates that Cambodia did not initiate the firing.

He insisted that international borders cannot be altered by force or through the creation of situations intended to compel tacit acceptance, while also calling for the joint demarcation of the Thai-Cambodian border.

According to Manet Cambodia-Thailand border is based on historical agreements and established demarcation, rejecting any attempts to alter the status quo through military operations or unilateral actions.

“Borders cannot be changed by force,” Hun Manet emphasized, adding that Cambodia would not accept any attempts to create new realities on the ground.

He reiterated that Cambodia remains committed to defending its sovereignty and territorial integrity through peaceful means and in accordance with international law.

MN202611_yvq49yi1ok.t:
Arsene Wenger had considered running for the Fifa presidency

Former Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger has decided not to stand against Gianni Infantino as a candidate in Fifa's presidential election.

The Frenchman had been considering running for the job but sources have told BBC Sport that he has ruled himself out.

Current world football chief Infantino's position was plunged into crisis by a backlash caused by his failed plan to sell commercial stakes in the World Cup to private investors.

Wenger - who is Fifa's head of global development - would have had the backing of European football's governing body Uefa, which has spearheaded opposition to Infantino.

On Saturday, French newspaper L'Equipe reported that Wenger was unlikely , external to challenge his boss.

Wenger has credibility throughout the footballing world, and this will be a significant boost to Infantino as he seeks a fourth term as president.

Uefa is said to still be hopeful of finding an alternative candidate before Wednesday's deadline.

One influential figure in the group of stakeholders opposed to Infantino told BBC Sport the news was "a real shame".

"Even if not perfect, I do think he could have galvanized many around the world," they added.

Infantino laughs off resignation questions

Former Tottenham defender Ramon Vega was the first person to put his name forward in October.

Japan Football Association honorary president Kozo Tashima has also announced his intention to stand.

However, sources have told BBC Sport that the 68-year-old has not yet secured the necessary five endorsements from member associations ahead of Wednesday's deadline but is "still fighting hard".

Amid the fallout over FFE, Wenger, who has traditionally been loyal to Infantino, distanced himself from the aborted plot.

"I was not involved in this strategic plan and first became aware of the project through media reports," Wenger said at the time.

"The decision to withdraw the project was absolutely necessary and beyond question, because I firmly believe in an independent Fifa that serves our game with commitment, transparency and integrity."

Infantino has retained support in South America, Africa and Asia, and recently insisted he has the backing of the "vast, vast majority" of world football.

MN202611_o4fqys60te.t:
In Cambodia kissing in Public, female and male hugging and also holding hands are guestures considered inappropriate.

However, President Emmanuel Macron of France caused a near cultural crash when he kissed a young Cambodian boy.

During his walk along Phnom Penh’s riverside last night, President Macron greeted a young Cambodian boy with a kiss on the cheek.

In France such a guesture is familiar, but less common in Cambodia.

While in Cambodia one is advised to avoid any physical intimacy near temples, schools, markets, or rural villages.

Kissing family members or loved ones on the lips or cheek is not standard practice in Cambodia.

Cambodia people traditionally greet or show affection with a hug or a traditional “sniff kiss” (pressing the nose to the cheek and inhaling gently).

Macron’s gesture has triggered a lengthy debate over local media outlets.

Cambodia is a conservative, Buddhist-majority society, public displays of affection (PDA) are considered disrespectful and offensive.

The French leader begun a tour of Southeast Asia with a 48-hour stop in Cambodia. He will be heading to Malaysia.

MN202611_zw50xpxxej.t:
Nine people were killed in the shooting at the Greek Orthodox church last month

A Jordanian court has sentenced three men to death by hanging for carrying out a fatal mass shooting on a church last month.

The attack on 23 October killed nine people and injured 34 others who had been attending a Christian funeral at a Greek Orthodox church in Karak governorate.

Jordan's Armed Forces said in a statement on Sunday that the men had been convicted of committing "terrorist acts", as well as possessing weapons, "promoting the ideas of a terrorist organisation" and "conspiracy to commit terrorist acts".

The three men - two Jordanian brothers and their brother-in-law - fled the scene of the attack and were arrested three days later. They have not been publicly identified.

Karak is home to a sizeable Christian community in the Muslim-majority kingdom.

CCTV footage from the day of the attack showed three men holding guns approaching and firing on St George's church in the village of Hmoud.

Watch: CCTV footage appears to show gunmen near church

A second video showed dead and wounded people lying on the ground amid chaotic scenes at the church.

It is still unclear why the attackers chose to target that specific church.

Shortly after the attack, Jordan's King Abdullah II wrote on X: "The terrorist attack against Karak will be met with the harshest retaliation.

"Those who delude themselves into thinking that they can divide Jordanians with their bullets have no chance in the face of our unity."

The three men fled the scene of the shooting and were later located inside an abandoned house in Karak governorate, south of the capital, Amman.

They refused to surrender and opened fire on security forces, who returned fire and wounded all three of them , the Public Security Directorate said at the time. No security personnel were hurt in the shootout.

King Abdullah praised security forces for chasing the suspects "to the very end".

The week after the Karak shooting, Jordan struck what its military said were "terrorist organisations" in Syria in retaliation to the church attack.

Syrian health officials told state media that five people, including women, children and an elderly man, were killed in the strike on a village in the southern Daraa province. Jordan said its fighter jets had killed and wounded "several terrorists" without giving further details.

Jordan said it had co-ordinated with the Syrian government, but Syria said it had not been notified in advance.

Executions in Jordan are carried out by hanging. The kingdom previously observed an unofficial ban on executions from 2006 to 2014, and another pause from 2017 until June this year.

Intwazangabo nkuru y'umuhari Hamas yafashije mu gutegura akanayobora igitero co ku wa 7 Gitugutu (10) 2023 muri Israel, yishwe mu gitero co mu kirere ca Israel, nk'uko abategetsi ba Israel nna Gaza babivuga.

Samir Abu Younis, yari aherutse kugenwa nk'umukuru wa Birigade (Brigade) ya Rafah, yiciwe ahitwa Al-Mawasi mu bumanuko bw'akarere ka Gaza ejo ku wa gatandatu, nk'uko bitangazwa n'ishami rya gisirikare rya Hamas, Brigades Al-Qassam.

Umutegetsi wa Hamas muri ako karere yemeje urupfu rwa Younis, igisirikare ca Israel na co kikaba cavuze ko ari we ico gitero cari kigambiriye neza neza, kandi ko imbere yaco hari "hafashwe ingingo zo kugabanya ingaruka ku basivire".

Ababibonye muri Gaza bavuga ko ibisasu bine vya misire vyarashwe kw'ihema ryo mw'ikambi ya Al-Waha ihaye indaro amajana n'amajana y'abateshejwe izabo muri Al-Mawasi, bituma haduka umuriro.

Isoko ryo mu bitaro vya Nasser biri mu gisagara ca Khan Younis rivuga ko ibi bitaro vyakiriye abantu batatu bakomeretse, hamwe n'ikiziga kimwe.

Mw'itangazo ryacishijwe ku rubuga rwa Telegram, Ingabo za Israel (IDF) hamwe n'urwego rw'umutekano rw'ico gihugu (ISA) bemeje ko bishe Younis.

Bavuga ko yari "umwe mu bantu bakomeye cane mu ndongozi za Hamas", kandi ko yari afise "intego yo kugerageza gusubiza inguvu Brigade ya Rafah hamwe n'umurwi w'iterabwoba wa Hamas".

Iri tangazo ryongerako riti: "Younis yarahaye amategeko abarwanyi ba Brigade yo gukora no kwongereza ibitero vy'iterabwoba ku basivire n'abasirikare ba Israel."

Amakuru ya BBC Gahuza ako kanya kuri WhatsApp yawe

Ku ruhande rwayo, Brigades Al-Qassam yanditse kuri Telegram ko Younis "yagize uruhara mu bikorwa vyinshi vyo ku rwego rwo hejuru, anatesha ibitero vy'umwansi", kandi ko yari "umwe mu ntwazangabo nkuru nkuru zagize uruhara mu gutegura no kuyobora igitero co ku wa 7 Gitugutu".

Iri shami rya gisirikare rya Hamas rivuga ko urupfu rwiwe ari "ubwicanyi bw'ububisha".

Younis w'imyaka 53 yari yatanguye amabanga yiwe ku wa 15 Nyakanga (9) 2025, inyuma y'urupfu rw'uwari arongoye Birigade ya Rafah, Nael Abu Obeid.

Yinjiye muri iri shami rya gisirikare rya Hamas mu 1991, arangura amabanga atandukanye yo ku rwego rwo hejuru imbere y'uko agenwa nk'umukuru w'iyo birigade. Hamas yavuze ko ibikorwa vyo kumushingura biza kuba kuri uno wa Mungu mu gisagara ca Khan Younis.

Igitero ca Hamas mu bumanuko bwa Israel ku wa 7 Gitugutu 2023, cahitanye abantu bashika ku 1.200 abandi 251 bagafatwa bugwati, ni co ntandaro y'intambara y'ubu bwa vuba muri Gaza.

Kuva ico gihe, abantu barenga 74.650 baramaze kwicwa muri ako karere kegukira ubutegetsi bwa Palestina, nk'uko ubushikiranganji bw'amagara y'abantu muri Gaza bubivuga.

Nubwo muri Gituguru 2025 habaye amasezerano yo guhagarika intambara, Israel irabandanya rimwe na rimwe n'ibitero ivuga ko bikorwa ku barwanyi ba Hamas bagisigaye, ikavuga ko ifise uburenganzira bwo kubarasa hisunzwe ibiri muri ayo masezerano.

Thailand is up in arms in total anger against Cambodia for dragging their border dispute into the La Francophonie Summit ongoing in Phnom Penh.

Days before the summit, Thailand warned Cambodia against using the Francophonie gathering to raise the border dispute. But Prime Minister Hun Manet went ahead anyway.

“Cambodia did not fire the first shot,” Premier Manet said in his opening remarks at the organisation’s Summit on Sunday.

Cambodia accuses Thai troops of continuing to occupy Cambodian territory.

Manet said the ceasefire reached on December 27 is holding, but the situation remains fragile.

He revealed that around 20,000 Cambodians fled and are still unable to return home.

Hun Manet called for existing agreements to be honored and joint border demarcation to resume.

However, Thailand warns that raising the dispute at the summit could undermine efforts to rebuild trust.

On the contrary to the ceasefire, Cambodia sources accuse Thailand of, “increasing military present, continue to dig trenches and fortified the contested area which clearly violated the temporary peace agreement made, and yet asked Cambodia to not say anything.”

French President Emmanuel Macron told Francophonie delegates at the ongoing Summit to seek for “unity” and “consensus” in resolving disputes.

“We must ensure that we preserve what makes it strong, namely its unity,” he adds.

La Francophonie leaders and various guests are being treated to a mouthwatering luncheon hosted by International Organisation of La Francophonie (OIF) Secretary-General Louise Mushikiwabo.

President Kagame and First Lady Jeannette Kagame joined other Heads of state and government for lunch.

After the luncheon, leaders return to conference hall and continue high-level negotiations and debates centered on the summit’s theme, “Reinvesting in Peace for Shared Prosperity and Sustainable Stability”.

On the line up, the leaders will review and adopt key consensus documents, including the Phnom Penh Declaration.

Later the OIF bloc members will continue with discussions and the decision-making process for the new Secretary-General for the upcoming term (with candidacies and alignments involving nations like Rwanda and the DRC drawing close attention).

On the other hand leaders and delegations at the Summit will conduct guided cultural visits, including tours to Siem Reap and Angkor (such as the inauguration of the restored West Mebon temple by King Norodom Sihamoni and French President Emmanuel Macron).

MN202611_l4csgzuuo1.t:
Without dialogue and consensus conflicts may drag on within the La Francophonie bloc, French President Emmanuel Macron said in his opening remarks at the 20th La Francophonie Summit in Phnom Penh, Cambodia.

President Macron called on member states to preserve the unity of OIF through dialogue and consensus.

“We must build consensus to preserve unity,” he stressed, advocating for a Francophonie that is united, committed and forward-looking.

Macron acknowledged that the Francophonie “is not spared from crises” and called for “building consensus” to preserve its unity.

Macron carefully avoided pointing fingers at any country or specifically mentioning an existing rift between some members of the bloc.

On Monday the Francophonie leaders will elect a new Secretary General of the organisation.

Rwanda one of smallest members and the Democratic Republic of Congo the world’s largest french speaking country have fielded candidates for the OIF Sec.Gen slot.

Throughout the campaigns for their candidates, the two countries have dragged Political disputes to Phnom Penh.

Kinshasa accuses Rwanda of aiding the FRN rebels who currently control large parts of North and South Kivu Provinces in East of the mineral rich country of over 100million people.

The DRC has been working so hard to prevent the Rwandan incumbent Louis Mushikiwabo from being re-elected.

The competition for the slot saw DRC field candidate Juliana Lumumba daughter of independence icon Patrice Lumumba.

Pte William Douglas Dal Bianco died from his injuries suffered at a Canadian military base last month

A fifth Canadian soldier has died from injuries he suffered when a grass fire swept through a military training area last month.

Four people were killed initially and dozens were injured when the fire, which ignited during a live fire training exercise, spread rapidly through Canadian Forces Base Wainwright carried by strong winds on 17 October.

Pte William Douglas Dal Bianco, who had been receiving medical care in Ontario, died on Friday, the Canadian Armed Forces said in a statement.

Prime Minister Mark Carney wrote on X: "Canadians are holding Private Dal Bianco's loved ones, and all those still grieving in the wake of this terrible tragedy, in our hearts."

The Canadian Armed Forces said that 24 military personnel were still in hospital receiving treatment, while 14 had been released as of Saturday. Thirty-eight military personnel had been injured in total.

Canadian Forces Base Wainwright in Alberta is one of the country's busiest military training bases

Members of 1 Canadian Mechanized Brigade Group had been conducting live-fire training at the base, in the province of Alberta, when the fire broke out.

Military officials said at the time that the fire spread across a kilometre in a matter of seconds, taking many of those on the base by surprise.

Firefighters battled the blaze through the night, while nearby hospitals became inundated by injured personnel and staff.

Carney described it as "one of the worst tragedies for the forces on Canadian soil in peacetime".

An investigation found that the fire was likely sparked by a grenade launcher being fired on the base's grenade range, officials said.

Firefighters on the base had known about the fire but could not tackle it because it was in a danger area that could contain unspent explosives.

Canadian Chief of the Defence Staff Gen Jennie Carignan said the nation's armed forces were "heartbroken" by the loss of Dal Bianco, while Defence Minister David McGuinty offered his "deepest condolences" to his family, friends and colleagues.

"No words can ease the pain of losing a loved one, and my thoughts remain with all those affected by this tragedy," he said.

"We remain committed to supporting the families and the Canadian Armed Forces community during this profoundly difficult time, and to honouring Private Dal Bianco's service, dedication and sacrifice to Canada."

Mu gihe hasigaye amasaha make ngo abakuru b'ibihugu n'ama reta bagize ishirahamwe mpuzamakungu ry'ibihugu bikoresha ururimi rw'Igifaransa (OIF) batore umunyamabanga mukuru mushasha i Phnom Penh muri Cambodge, amaso ya benshi ntari gusa ku bariko barondera kwitoza. Ahubwo yerekejwe ku migenderanire mibi hagati y'ibihugu bibanyi vy'Urwanda na Repubulika ya Demokrasi ya Congo (RDC).

Urwanda na Congo vyompi bifise aba candida muri bane bifuza kurongora uwo muryango w'ibihugu 53:

Kuba Urwanda na RD Congo vyompi bifise abakandida, ivyo gutora umunyamabanga mushasha wa OIF vyahindutse urugamba rwa dipolomasi muri iryo shirahamwe.

Ariko muri abo bane, amaso yose ari kuri Mushikiwabo.

RD Congo imaze igihe ica ku biti no ku mabuye kugira ngo izibire Mushikiwabo ngo ntatorwe. Kandi yitwaza igihagararo cayo mu muryango. Ni gihugu kirusha ibindi vyinshi mu bantu miriyoni 300 bavuga canke bakoresha ururimi rw'igifaransa kw'isi.

Muri RD Congo, hari abanyaporitike babona ko bitabereye kandi bitumvikana ko igihugu cagirizwa gushigikira umuhari w'inyeshamba zirwanya ubutegetsi bw'igihugu cabo cobandanya kirongoye rimwe mu mashirahamwe akomeye kw'isi y'abakoresha igifaransa.

Nubwo ata tangazo ryasohowe ku mugaragaro, bamwe mu bategetsi ba Congo bagiye berekana ko ari nka hamwe Mushikiwabo yosubira gutorwa ngo arongore Francophonie, igihugu cabo cova muri iryo shirahamwe, canke kigasubira kwihweza nimba koko cobandanya kiri umunywanyi wayo.

Abajijwe n'imboneshakure TV5 Monde ico avuga kuri ibi, Mushikiwabo yishuye ati: "Naravyumvise koko, ariko jewe ubwanje vyontangaza cane…Muri OIF nta gihugu gifise uburenganzira bwo guhagarika canke kwanka ingingo y'abandi. Ingingo zose zishingira ku nzira yemejwe kandi yemerwa n'ibihugu vyose bigize iri shirahamwe.

"Jewe rero vyontangaza cane. Congo ni igihugu gikomeye ku buryo kitofata ingingo y'ishavu".

N'ubwo umushikiranganji wa Congo ajejwe imigenderanire Therese Kayikwamba atabivuga mu majambo yeruye, yavuze ko mu gutora canke kugena umunyamabanga mukuru mushasha hoshirwa imbere kwumvikana kugira abanywanyi b'ishirahamwe birinde kuwushira mu "cuka kibi".

Amakuru ya BBC Gahuza ako kanya kuri WhatsApp yawe

Mu kimeze nko gutanga akarorero keza, igihe haba ibirori vyo kwugurura iyi nama ejo ku wa gatandatu, umushikiranganji w'imigenderanire n'ayandi makungu wa RD Congo, Thérèse Kayikwamba Wagner, yavuze ko igihugu ciwe citeguye kwemera gusokora ikarata ya Juliana Lumumba yo kwitoza mu ntumbero yo kworohereza umwumvikano ku wotorwa.

Ku bwa Kayikwamba, ico ni ikimenyetso c'uko igihugu ciwe gishira imbere ubumwe bw'ishirahamwe kuruta inyungu zaco bwite, agasaba n'ibindi bihugu gukurikira iyo nzira.

N'aho bitavuzwe gutyo, bisa no kuvuga ngo "nderekanye umutima mwiza wo kwirinda ingorane, uwundi nagire nk'uko". Uwo wundi rero ni Urwanda.

Imboneshakure Africa 24 isubiramwo amajambo yiwe agira ati: "Turizigiye kandi ko iki cemezo twafashe kizotuma abagize iri shirahamwe bose basubira kwihweza ivyiyumviro vyabo, maze bongere bashire imbere inyungu rusangi n'inyungu z'ishirahamwe kuruta inyungu z'umuntu umwe canke iz'igihugu ciwe."

Abajijwe icoba ari nka hamwe Urwanda rutokora nka RDC, yishuye ati: "Nimba Urwanda rutabigize, ruzoba rwafashe ingingo yarwo kandi ni rwo ruyibazwa. Ntituri ngaha kugira ngo duhatire abandi gufata uruhande uru canke ruriya, turi ngaha kugira dusigure kandi twunganire ivyiyumviro vyacu, ariko kandi twubahe kandi twemere ko n'abandi bafise ivyiyumviro vyabo."

Nta kimenyetso urundi ruhande rurerekana. Louise Mushikiwa yabwiye ikinyamakuru TV5 ko ari "umukandida gushika ku ka nyuma", nawe umushikiranganji wiwe ajejwe imigenderanire Olivier Nduhungirehe avuga ko ivyo Congo yatangaje bitanze inzira yo kwerekeza amaso ku mukandida abikwiye, ni ukuvuga Mushikiwabo.

Mw'ijambo ryo kwugurura inama y'abakuru b'ibihugu, umukuru w'igihugu c'Ubufaransa Emmanuel Macron yirinze kugaruka mu majambo yeruye kuri ico cuka kiri mu muryango imbere y'uko haba amatora. Ariko nawe nyene yasavye ko haba umwumvikano nk'uko bisanzwe ari vyo bishirwa imbere muri OIF.

Amakuru avuga ko Perezida Macron yoba yipfuza ko haboneka uwundi yokwumvikanwako kugira yitoze, uwuvugwa cane akaba ari Umu-Roumanie Dacian Cioloș, ibi na vyo bikaba bitashimishije bamwe mu bategetsi b'Urwanda.

Abajijwe na TV 5 Monde nimba yoba afata ko ibisabwa na Perezida Macron ari ukwivanga mu bitamuraba, Louise Mushikiwabo yishuye ati: "Biragaragara, biragaragara, ariko umuntu ategerezwa kumenya ingene avyifatamwo".

Ibi bituma aya matora buca aba ahinduka nk'igipimo c'ijambo mu migenderanire (diplomacie) buri gihugu gifise ku rubuga mpuzamakungu.

Ariko azoba kandi n'igipimo c'ubumwe hagati y'ibihugu vya Afrika.

Mw'ishirahamwe rya Afrika (Union Africaine) vyari bisanzwe vyarumvikanywe ko igihe cose haba hari uwitoza w'umunyafrika, mu kibanza mpuzamakungu, ibihugu vyose biheza bikamushigikira. OIF irimwo ibihugi vya Afrika barenga 20.

Rero muri aya matora buca aba, amatati hagati y'ibi bihugu bibiri bidahengeshanya kwitana ba mwana ariko araboneka ko ari co kibazo nyamukuru, mbere cagumye kigaruka, hakaba hari n'abagifata ko ari igipimo kuri kazoza ka Francophonie.

Hari ababona ko mu gihe Mushikiwabo yoramuka asubiriye gutorwa vyoca vyerekana ububasha bukomeye bwa Kigali mu bijanye n'imigenderanire mpuzamakungu, ariko kandi hakaba n'abandi babona ko mu gihe atotorwa kubera gusa ko ari Umunyarwandakazi, Congo nayo yoba yerekanye inguvu z'ijwi ryayo.

Ku ruhande rwa Mushikiwabo n'Urwanda, ni uko OIF idakwiye guhindurwa urubuga rw'imishamirano hagati y'ibihugu bibiri, mu gihe Repubulika ya Demokarasi ya Congo yoyo ibandanya yerekana ko ishirahamwe rivuga ko rishingiye ku mabwirizwa yo kwubahiriza ubusugire bw'ibihugu, demokarasi n'ukwubahana hagati y'ibihugu birigize ridakwiye kwirengagiza ihoyangwa ry'izo ngingo.

Ivyo ari vyo vyose, ibishobora kuva mu matora ategekanijwe i Phnom Penh bishobora kuzokwerekana ishusho n'igihagararo ca OIF imbere y'ibibazo bihanze isi, hamwe n'ingaruka amatati hagati y'ibihugu ashobora kugira kuri kazoza k'ishirahamwe.

Cambodia’s Capital city authorities along with the Interdepartmental Association for Sanitation in the Paris Region (SIAAP) and the International Association of Francophone Mayors (AIMF) – signed a joint letter of intent to extend their partnership and support the second phase of the capital’s septage management project.

The agreement follows the successful completion and launch of the first phase in 2023.

The signing ceremony was attended by Phnom Penh Governor Khuong Sreng, AIMF Delegate General Frederic Vallier and SIAAP Director-General Valérie Molet.

The municipality’s Deputy Director of Administration and spokeswoman Dor Samphors said cooperation began in 2020 with support from the Seine-Normandy Water Agency (AESN).

The first phase resulted in the construction of the capital’s first septage treatment plant in Kambol district, alongside the development of institutional management structures and regulatory frameworks.

The project’s final evaluation report in 2025 highlighted tangible achievements while identifying the need to further expand Phnom Penh’s septage treatment capacity in the years ahead, she noted.

Building on the results of the first phase and aligning with the municipal administration’s strategic plan through 2035, the second phase will involve constructing another treatment plant in Meanchey district and conducting a feasibility study in preparation for a possible third facility.

The estimated budget for the second phase is approximately €2.32 million (about $2.56 million), excluding in-kind contributions.

Funding is expected to come from the AIMF, AESN, SIAAP and the Phnom Penh Capital Administration.

The second phase is scheduled to begin after the technical working group completes detailed discussions on the cooperation agreement and participating parties formally sign it in the near future.

One of the camps in Al-Mawasi in southern Gaza

A senior Hamas figure who helped plan and oversee the 7 October 2023 attack on Israel has been killed in an Israeli airstrike, officials in Israel and Gaza have said.

Samir Abu Younis, the newly appointed commander of the Rafah Brigade, was killed on Saturday in Al-Mawasi in the southern Gaza Strip, according to Hamas's Al-Qassam Brigades military wing.

A local Hamas official confirmed Younis's death. The Israeli military said it had targeted him and that prior to the strike "steps were taken to mitigate harm to civilians".

Eyewitnesses in Gaza said four missiles struck a tent in the Al-Waha camp, which shelters hundreds of displaced people in Al-Mawasi, causing a fire to break out.

A medical source at Nasser Hospital in the southern city of Khan Younis said three injured people had arrived there, as well as a dead body.

The Israel Defence Forces (IDF) and Israel's security agency, the ISA, confirmed in a statement on Telegram that it had "eliminated" Younis.

Describing him as a "central figure among Hamas's senior figures", it said he had "acted with the aim of trying to restore the strength of the brigade and the Hamas terrorist organisation".

It added: "Younis directed the brigade's terrorists to advance and carry out terror attacks against Israeli civilians and IDF troops."

Al-Qassam Brigades wrote on Telegram that Younis had "participated in numerous high-profile operations and resisted enemy incursions", and was "one of the most important commanders involved in planning and overseeing the 7 October attack".

It described his killing as a "cowardly assassination".

Younis, 53, had been in his position since 15 September, following the death of the brigade's previous commander, Nael Abu Obeid.

He joined Hamas' armed wing in 1991 and held several senior operational roles before becoming commander. His funeral will be held on Sunday afternoon in Khan Younis, Hamas said.

The Hamas-led attack on southern Israel on 7 October 2023, when about 1,200 people were killed an 251 others taken hostage, triggered the most recent war in Gaza.

Since then, more than 74,650 people have been killed in the Palestinian territory, the health ministry there says.

Though a ceasefire was reached last October, Israel has continued strikes it says are targeting remaining Hamas militants, which it argues it has the right to do under the terms of the ceasefire agreement.

More than 1,640 people have been killed in Gaza since the October 2025 ceasefire, according to the territory's health ministry, whose figures are considered reliable by the UN.

Update November 15: An earlier version of this article referred to Israel carrying out 'occasional' strikes in Gaza following a ceasefire in October 2025. This word has been removed to better reflect the frequency of Israeli strikes on Gaza since the ceasefire.

Peter Schmeichel handed Unai Simon the Yashin Trophy and the room applauded warmly. Then the world's best goalkeeper spent his time talking about everybody else.

Simon thanked his parents and his brother. He thanked his girlfriend for being an "oasis of tranquillity", and the friends from home who remind him that "many of us in this room are privileged".

'La cuadrilla', the gang of lifelong friends that is a traditional part of Basque culture, has a WhatsApp group of its own, and he takes them on holiday every summer.

He thanked his coaches and team-mates. Like Simon, none of them are regulars on the covers of the media.

Then he talked about a man who could not be in the room at last month's Ballon d'Or ceremony in London, but whose influence lives on - Simon's youth academy mentor Koldo Asua, who died in 2021.

The Spain and Athletic Club number one is not your archetypal superstar. In fact, he is the complete opposite.

He stays away from the headlines and is relatively low profile when compared with some of the game's other goalkeepers. His position as Spain's number is regularly questioned - as was the decision to name him as the world's best.

In the part-beauty pageant election that is the Ballon d'Or, being low key can work against you, but the case on the pitch is easy to state - even though it rattles those who see the Premier League as the highest standard reachable.

Was Raya robbed & how did Europe react to Kane's Ballon d'Or win?

Unai Simon was named the world's best goalkeeper at the recent Ballon d'Or ceremony

Back to the award. Most acceptance speeches are lists of names. This one drew a portrait of a man, and it explains why the voters got it right.

Simon's mentor Asua spent 13 years in Bilbao working with young Athletic Club players, helping them keep their family ties and their studies alive next to football.

Simon told the Palladium Asua changed how he understood the game, and that what matters is "the legacy one leaves when this is over" - being remembered as a good person and a good team-mate.

He then turned to ex-Spain and Athletic goalkeeper Jose Angel Iribar, 83 years old and still an ambassador for the club.

Iribar, who holds the all-time appearances record at Athletic with 614 matches, wore black as a homage to legendary goalkeeper Levin Yashin - the Russian 'Black Spider' - and Simon wears the same colour as a tribute to Iribar.

Simon's parents also got a mention, because they raised him with values later reinforced at Athletic: respect for authority, a work ethic and keeping close to people who love you.

Before Spain's World Cup final triumph, Simon spoke about the natural order in which other goalkeepers could soon replace him. Arsenal's David Raya is one of those players in that queue.

Before England's Nations League visit to Spain on Sunday, Simon keeps his place with that competition beside him. Raya and Joan Garcia must wait for their moment to take the number one shirt of the best national team in the world.

Spain won the World Cup and Simon conceded the fewest goals during the tournament, which earned him the Golden Glove.

He conceded a single goal in the whole competition and kept seven clean sheets. His longest run without conceding lasted about 650 minutes, beating the 517-minute record of Italy's Walter Zenga at the 1990 tournament.

After the tournament, Simon talked about not having had much to do.

"If my gloves could talk, they would say they have not worked as hard as other goalkeepers' gloves," he said. As if it had all been that easy.

The team trusts him so much they know he will be there when needed, and his involvement in build-up is part of how Spain play.

Behind that summer sits a longer body of work: the Nations League, the European Championship and, in 2023-24, the Zamora Trophy - given to the keeper with the lowest goals conceded to games ratio in Spain - the first for an Athletic goalkeeper since Iribar in 1970.

Unai Simon has won the World Cup, European Championship and Nations League with Spain

He has not had it easy. Simon was born in Vitoria in 1997, grew up in the village of Murgia and joined Athletic's academy in 2011, aged 14.

In 2018 Athletic sold Kepa Arrizabalaga to Chelsea, and Simon, a young goalkeeper out of Basconia and Bilbao Athletic, who had been sent on loan to Elche, became first choice almost by accident.

An injury to the number two Iago Herrerin, and the refusal of Alejandro Remiro to renew his contract, brought Simon back to Bilbao after only 20 days at Elche.

Many thought he would be a temporary solution. He made the position his own, and a year later he won the Under-21 European Championship with Spain. The coach? Luis de la Fuente.

His game has grown as well. Luis Enrique saw he could play with his feet and was patient with him, and Simon says the rest took a lot of analysis and training and a bit of courage.

There were doubts along the way. During the last Nations League, even De la Fuente said Simon had been badly treated for a long time, and the coach kept picking him.

Now Simon has been voted the best. He collected 351 points in the Ballon d'Or voting and finished 128 ahead of Raya in second place, with Thibaut Courtois third. Two years ago he had come second to Emi Martinez with 213 points, and last year he was not among the 10 nominees.

By his own account he is shy with people he does not know. He says he likes to "stay away from the hustle and bustle", yet friends and neighbours back home say he is the opposite with the people he does know.

He has no social media account any more, because he read everything written about him and let it decide how he felt, terrible after the bad comments and brilliant after the good ones.

The choice that explains the rest came in 2024. Simon signed a contract to 2029 with no release clause and said he wanted to be the best goalkeeper in the world as part of Athletic.

"I owe the life I have to Athletic," he said. Athletic's Basque-only policy means there is no Champions League every year and individual awards are difficult to get. But now he is the first Spanish goalkeeper to win the Yashin Trophy.

When he was small there was no drinking water in his village, and he often helped his grandparents fill the jugs from the water tanker.

On one of his latest visits, he arrived in the car he has driven for eight years, gathered all the village children and took them for a kickabout.

That is what he did with his biggest night: he gave it away to others.

Do you still think that the boy who used to tear his trousers diving on dirt pitches and on asphalt, to his mother's despair, does not deserve the prize?

Perezida wa Repubulika y’u Rwanda, Paul Kagame, na Madamu Jeannette Kagame, bitabiriye umuhango wo gutangiza ku mugaragaro Inama ya 20 y’Abakuru b’Ibihugu na za Guverinoma bihuriye mu Muryango w’Ibihugu bikoresha Igifaransa (OIF), wabereye i Phnom Penh muri Cambodia.

Uyu muhango wabaye mu gitondo cyo ku wa 15 Ugushyingo 2026, ubera muri Chroy Changvar International Convention and Exhibition Centre, witabirwa n’Umwami wa Cambodia, Norodom Sihamoni, Minisitiri w’Intebe Hun Manet, Umunyamabanga Mukuru wa OIF, Louise Mushikiwabo, hamwe n’abandi bakuru b’ibihugu na za guverinoma.

Inama y’uyu mwaka yakiriwe na Leta ya Cambodia, ikaba ihurije hamwe abayobozi bagamije kuganira ku bibazo byugarije isi no gushaka ibisubizo bihuriweho, hibandwa ku mahoro, umutekano, iterambere n’ubufatanye mpuzamahanga.

Umunyamabanga Mukuru wa OIF, Louise Mushikiwabo, na we yashimangiye ko amahoro ari umutungo ukomeye usaba kwitabwaho buri munsi.

Yagize ati: “Amahoro ni umutungo wubakwa buhoro buhoro, ariko ukangirika vuba kandi ugasaba kwitabwaho buri munsi.” Agaragaje ko Cambodia, nyuma y’imyaka myinshi y’intambara n’ibibazo byayiranze, izi neza agaciro k’amahoro.

Mu bandi bayobozi batanze ubutumwa muri uyu muhango harimo Umunyamabanga Mukuru w’Umuryango w’Abibumbye, António Guterres, washimangiye ko Francophonie ifite uruhare rukomeye mu kubaka icyizere, guteza imbere amahoro no gushyigikira iterambere rirambye.

Guterres yavuze ko ururimi ruhuriweho n’ibihugu rufasha gukomeza ubufatanye hagati y’abaturage n’ibihugu. Yagize ati: “Ururimi ruhuriweho ni igishoro cy’icyizere. Icyizere ni umutungo ukomeye kurusha iyindi, kandi tugomba kuwukomeza.”

Yashimiye kandi OIF ku bufatanye yagiranye n’Umuryango w’Abibumbye mu guteza imbere amahoro, iterambere rirambye no kubahiriza uburenganzira bwa muntu.

Inama ya 20 ya Francophonie ifite insanganyamatsiko igira iti “Kongera gushora imbaraga mu mahoro hagamijwe iterambere risangiwe n’umutekano urambye” (Reinvest in Peace for Shared Prosperity and Lasting Stability).

Iyi nama izamara iminsi ibiri, kuva ku wa 15 kugeza ku wa 16 Ugushyingo 2026, ikaba ihuje abahagarariye ibihugu na za guverinoma 90 bigize umuryango wa Francophonie, hagamijwe kurebera hamwe uko ubufatanye mu bya dipolomasi, ubukungu, umuco, uburezi n’umutekano bwakomeza gutezwa imbere.

Kimwe mu byitezwe muri iyi nama ni amatora y’Umunyamabanga Mukuru mushya wa OIF azaba ku wa 16 Ugushyingo 2026. Louise Mushikiwabo, usanzwe ayobora uyu muryango kuva mu 2019, ari mu bakandida bahatanira gukomeza izi nshingano muri manda ya 2027–2030.

Kuba Perezida Kagame na Madamu Jeannette Kagame bitabiriye iyi nama bigaragaza uruhare rw’u Rwanda mu bikorwa by’uyu muryango, cyane cyane mu biganiro bigamije guteza imbere ururimi rw’Igifaransa, ubufatanye hagati y’ibihugu n’ibisubizo ku bibazo mpuzamahanga.

Aston Villa currently sit ninth in the Women's Super League table

A club's true identity always shows in a local derby and Aston Villa hope to impose theirs when they face rivals Birmingham City on Sunday.

Villa have not had a smooth ride of it this season after a winless start led to the sacking of former manager Natalia Arroyo at the end of September.

The Spaniard helped stabilise Villa during her two years in charge but they lacked consistency, and it left some wondering what their identity really was.

Brian Sorensen is the man in charge of changing that on the pitch now, while there are others off it who are transforming Villa behind the scenes.

"Aston Villa is a club of heart. We put a lot into everything we do," managing director Maggie Murphy told BBC Sport.

"I think a lot of people know we try to do everything the right way, the proper way. We're a club that is the heart of 'proper football' in many ways."

So what are Villa doing this season to get in touch with their values?

Find interviews and extra content on the BBC Women's Football Weekly feed

Former Everton boss Brian Sorensen is now managing Aston Villa

Sunday's Women's Super League match with Birmingham (14:00 GMT) marks 30 years since the team officially took the Aston Villa name.

Sorensen hoes it will be the perfect opportunity to showcase who Villa are on the pitch.

"There's a lot of history in this club which maybe not many people know. We need to showcase that," said interim manager Sorensen.

"We want to be really hard-working and humble - like the area we are from - and have a clear identity of how we attack and defend.

"It's trying to align all of that, making sure that we are a team that is recognised, that is one the other teams will fear playing against."

They will celebrate this crucial point in their history in the second city derby at Villa Park, and inform fans of a research project they are undertaking this season.

The project is called 'Roots, Rise and Reach' and hopes to uncover periods of the women's team's history that have never been documented before.

They have already found a newspaper report from 1957 detailing a game between an unofficial Aston Villa Ladies team and Birmingham City.

"It's huge piece of work that we're doing just to understand our own heritage and where we've come from," said Murphy.

"We're very aware that our roots go much further [than 1996]. We're going back decades at the moment trying to uncover some of that history.

"I think it's really important to know where we've come from, because that gives us a sense of identity that maybe we don't always have."

Diving into the club's history is one way Villa are hoping to engage fans this season.

They are trying to grow attendances as part of the club's five-year strategy and last season set up fan forums for the first time.

In response to feedback, they have changed age categories on their ticketing, introduced hospitality season tickets and hosted podcasts with former players and comedians to improve matchday experiences.

They have also been advertising upcoming games on 'digi-vans' throughout the country in the hope of attracting neutral women's football fans.

"There are plenty of floating fans in women's football so we are trying to grab as many as we can and make sure they have the best possible day," added Murphy.

"They might not support Villa the first time they come, but they might after three, four games and buy themselves a claret and blue scarf.

"That's our drive. We want to build this club sustainably and generate the funds that can then go into the football side of the business."

Villa players are happy stop to sign autographs and take photos after games

All of these efforts are part of a wider club ambition to be sustainable and ultimately deliver success on the pitch.

Murphy's task is to make the women's team financially stable, drive revenue and improve atmosphere at games.

She works in tandem with Marisa Ewers, director of women's football, who oversees recruitment, contract renewals and football staff management.

"We want it to be super coherent across both sides. In a really crude way, my job is to make money and Marissa's job is to spend it," said Murphy.

"Our teams work really closely together. Last year, we only had two people in the club that were 100% dedicated to the women's business side. Today, we have nine.

"We are investing in revenue-generating areas. I definitely want us to be competing at the highest possible level consistently, but with heart.

"We want to feel like we have contributed to the story of women's football in this country."

Villa's season is starting to look up. They currently sit ninth with two wins and four draws from their opening nine matches.

They drew with Arsenal at the start of this month after beating Birmingham City in a penalty shootout in their Women's League Cup tie.

With successive matches against newly promoted sides Birmingham and Charlton coming up, can Villa take a step closer to where they want to be?

"Where we are today is born of the hard work of lots of people that have come before us. We need to recognise that and start to steady the ship," said Murphy.

"Villa has not been in the WSL for that long. People forget that. We're still in a very transitional phase - as is the wider women's football ecosystem."

An interactive reproduction of a self portrait by Kyffin Williams will allow visitors to feel the texture of the thick oil he used in his paintings

For the first time, the paintings of Sir Kyffin Williams have been brought to life in a new immersive experience at the National Library of Wales.

Technology similar to that used for exhibitions of Van Gogh, Cézanne and LS Lowry will immerse visitors in the mountain landscapes, hillfarms and stormy seas created by the painter, who is considered the defining Welsh artist of the 20th Century.

Images from Williams's oil paintings such as the hill farmer and sheepdog are animated in a 360-degree centrepiece and Sir Kyffin's life story is narrated by Sir Bryn Terfel in a bilingual presentation, with original paintings illuminated on the walls.

The National Library, which received grants of £500,000 to fund the project, said it hoped it will introduce a new audience to Sir Kyffin's work.

There are also interactive installations including a recreation of a self-portrait which can be touched, giving visitors a sense of the texture of Sir Kyffin's oil paintings.

He painted using an impasto technique - where paint is applied so thickly on to a canvas that it stands out in three dimensions.

Sir Kyffin, who was born on Anglesey in 1918, had a long relationship with the National Library, in Aberystwyth, Ceredigion, which has about 2,000 pieces of his work in its collection.

Moving images taken from Sir Kyffin's paintings are projected on to walls in what used to be an office in the national library

In 1950 the library bought its first two pieces from the young artist soon after he left the Slade School of Fine Art in London.

Morfudd Bevan, art curator at the National Library of Wales, said the library paid £15 for an oil painting of Cader Idris and £7.10 for an ink and wash drawing of Tre'r Ceiri on the Llŷn Peninsula.

Today, original work by Sir Kyffin sells for tens of thousands of pounds.

Bevan added: "The library saw the potential of this young artist.

"It was really important that we were encouraging and supporting young artists at the beginning of their careers, when Kyffin was trying to establish himself as a professional artist."

It was the start of a close bond with the artist.

When he died in September 2006, he left a substantial part of his estate to the library, more than 1,200 works on paper, about 200 oil paintings, more than 300 original prints and his personal archive.

The national library holds the largest collection of Sir Kyffin's work in the world.

Morfudd Bevan said the national library has a long relationship with Sir Kyffin Williams - it bought two pieces from him for £22 at the start of his career

The library hopes the new attraction will introduce more people to his work.

Director of experience Carys Ifan said: "It's by no means a traditional exhibition.

"You go on a journey, literally moving through three rooms that used to be old offices. They've been repurposed because we are so keen to open up more and more to the public."

Profiad Kyffin Experience was made possible by technology invented by Focal Studios, an immersive experience company and the main designers of the exhibition.

Chief executive Dennis Outten said working on the project had been a "labour of love" and an "incredible journey for everyone involved".

In the first room Sir Bryn Terfel tells the story of Sir Kyffin's life in a biligual narration while images taken from his work are projected on to the walls

Focal Studios worked with another company, leo&hyde, to animate Sir Kyffin's paintings in a 360-degree immersive experience so they come alive in projections on the walls and floor.

"It's like you're in one of his paintings, I love it," Outten said.

"It's not like virtual reality, because you can hold the hand of your child, you can sit there with your grandmother or your friend and you experience it together. I think that's incredibly powerful."

Inside the "projection cave", visitors see scenes painted by Sir Kyffin come alive as the cattle, waterfalls, the farmer and his sheepdog move around them.

Outten said high fidelity scans of Sir Kyffin's original work and creative techniques helped bring the paintings to life.

"We actually created a 3D model of Kyffin's farmer and dog, and then using animation techniques, puppeteering them essentially to move."

Rhodri Llwyd Morgan, the library's chief executive, said the new experience was part of a strategy "to be more popular, more appealing and that's our aim".

The experience was formally launched on Thursday and opens to the public from 18 November

Shane MacGowan was best known as the frontman of The Pogues, a band that injected rural folk songs with the punk spirit of the 1970s

On the day of Shane MacGowan's funeral , his heartbroken wife found comfort in the same thing that moved and captivated the rest of the world that afternoon - the music that filled a parish church in Nenagh, County Tipperary.

Mundy and Camille O'Sullivan performed Haunted. Nick Cave sang A Rainy Night in Soho. And Glen Hansard and Lisa O'Neil led mourners in a send-off rendition of Fairytale of New York .

"I thought, well, if we just got all the people who were at the funeral on a record, that'd be something pretty special," Victoria Mary Clarke told BBC News NI.

On Friday, three years after her husband's death, that idea came to fruition with the release of 20th Century Paddy.

"It must be wonderful for Shane... I think up in heaven, he's very aware of what's going on," said Clarke.

There are 36 tracks on the new album - all penned by MacGowan - and 40 bands and soloists.

Among those are contributions from two acclaimed Irish artists who have passed away since recording their covers for the album.

Glen Hansard is featured performing Bottle of Smoke, while Moya Brennan provides her interpretation of Mother Mo Chroi.

"I feel love and connection between the artists (on the album) and Shane.

"And also, you know, for me personally, it feels like a lot of love because when somebody sends something nice to Shane, they're sending it to me."

The Pogues frontman died aged 65 at his Dublin home in 2023, following a hospital stay after being diagnosed with encephalitis.

Shane MacGowan and Victoria Mary married in 2018 after several decades as a couple

Victoria was too fair to say who delivered her favourite cover on the album, but she was frank about how she personally benefited from the project.

"It gave me so much pleasure and it gave me so much joy and hope for the future to work on it because it gave me something to do every single day for three years and it got me out of bed and it got me to make new friends."

In the aftermath of her husband's death, that "social life and a sense of purpose" was invaluable to her.

But while the album is certainly bound up with MacGowan's death, it's not overshadowed by it.

"I think the artwork, if I had to pick, might be my favourite thing about the album," she chirped, an artist herself.

Bruce Springsteen spent time with Shane MacGowan at his home before his death

The term a 'who's who' doesn't quite capture the calibre and genre-defying diversity of the line-up featured on 20th Century Paddy.

There are hall-of-famers like Bruce Springsteen and Tom Waits.

Iconic, generation-crossing indie bands like The Jesus and Mary Chain and The Libertines.

And for anyone who needs reminding of how far above its weight Ireland punches when it comes to music, have a look at the back of 20th Century Paddy.

U2, Hozier and Bob Geldof - people with permanent residencies at top of the music industry.

There are stalwarts and custodians of the Irish folk tradition, Damien Dempsey perhaps foremost among them.

And lots of other artists, less established but very much in their ascendancy - Amble, Kingfishr and Madra Salach, to name but a few.

David Keenan said Shane MacGowan serves as an example of the importance of authenticity in art

David Keenan, a singer-songwriter from Dundalk, whose thoughtful lyrics and intense live performances invoke something of MacGowan himself, told BBC News NI he was honoured to be asked to add to the album.

"Fairytale of New York is as old as Christmas for me," said David.

But his epiphany moment came when an uncle gave him The Pogues' third album.

At 11 years old, Keenan said If I Should Fall from Grace with God "lit a flame" inside him.

"Up 'til that point it was just chart music.

"That (album) was the first time I heard all these references to mythology and drink and rebellion and, you know, heartache.

The Louth man described it like an awakening.

"It gave me permission as a kid to get stuck into real lyric writing. And to do it in the traditional and folk form."

On 20th Century Paddy, Keenan covered Sick Bed of Cúchulainn - a celtic punk ballad from their 1985 album Rum Sodomy and the Lash, the central allusion of which is the mythical Irish warrior Cúchulainn.

This has real significance for Keenan, who as a child in Louth used to play near the standing stone (Clochafarmore) where Cuchulainn was said to have been killed.

He did his recording of the song in Drumlish, County Longford, where he said "Shane used to record too".

"It was just was surreal and at the same time perfect, you know."

Before putting his version down on tape, Keenan did something few artists would have done: he recited a poem he had written in Irish asking permission from MacGowan to sing the song.

"I felt connected to Shane's energy during the recording, you know."

Keenan said the quality of the artists on 20th Century Paddy showed the "global respect that was there for Shane's abilities, you know, as a lyric writer, a poet".

He added that, at a time when there is "a lot of pressure on young musicians now to go viral on TikTok and dumb themselves down... here's an artist who didn't do that".

"In an age of ChatGPT and generative AI", said Keenan, MacGowan is a reminder for "human beings to be authentic".

Keenan's top picks from the album included Summer in Siam covered by Tom Waits, Jimmy Artache's version of USA, Glenn Hansard's Bottle of Smoke and Steve Earle's If I Should Fall From Grace With God.

But, given the quality on the album, the list, he said, could have gone on... and on... and on.

Michael says he did "a lot of practising" for his stand-up debut

Stepping onto the stage for the first time, Michael Hart is "flying" with adrenaline.

He didn't think he had it in him, but he's about to tell his own jokes to a room full of strangers.

He stutters at first but soon gets his first laugh from the crowd and the nerves he's feeling are washed away by a wave of elation.

Michael is part of a group of people who have struggled with mental ill-health and are now giving stand-up a go to build up their self-belief and connect with others.

Through the Finding Our Funny workshops run by the charity Inspire, they're turning their experiences into comedy material - and then taking it on the road for three gigs across Northern Ireland this month.

The comics have performed gigs in Enniskillen, Londonderry and Belfast

Michael has sought help for his mental health over the past few years and has struggled with his confidence.

Given those circumstances, throwing himself into stand-up is a daunting prospect - but he's embraced the challenge.

"The first thing I said was: 'What's the worst that can go wrong?

"I did stutter at the start, I sort of froze - but I came back in again. Just a joy to get up there. I think I kept it together well.

"My wee trick was I done a lot of practising."

He's now performed three gigs, using all his own material.

"It's all true, I didn't make any of this stuff up."

Carla Sloan says she's had mental health issues for most of her adult life and had never imagined trying her hand at stand-up until now.

"I've done lots of mental health courses on emotional resilience and stuff but this was something completely different.

"The first day I drove into the car park and then I was like: 'No.'

"I turned the car around and I drove back down the road and then I thought: 'Ah, I'm here, I might as well go in and see what it's about'."

Carla says her stand-up experience has boosted her self-esteem

As a mum of teenagers, Carla's jokes are about her real-life experiences of parenting.

"All my material is based on teenage girls and the fun you have raising them but also when they do something that they aren't meant to do," she smiles.

Tim McGarry is a veteran of the Northern Ireland comedy scene, best known for playing Da in the long-running BBC sitcom Give My Head Peace.

For decades he's given audiences the giggles with his own stand-up shows, so who better to mentor this bunch of budding comics?

For McGarry, the approach to comedy should be a simple one.

Tim McGarry shared some of his tricks of the trade, such as comic timing and dealing with a crowd

"I just sat down with them and said, well, what makes you laugh? What's something funny in your life?

"Most of them went off and wrote stuff themselves and I tweaked a bit and helped a wee bit - but it's coming from entirely the participants themselves."

While some comic techniques can be taught, McGarry says, much of his work as a mentor involved building their self-belief.

Getting "out of their comfort zone" and taking that first step onto the stage is the hard part, says McGarry - but the payoff is worth it.

"There is no better feeling than coming off stage and going: 'You know what? I made people laugh'."

Michael is keen to keep his stand-up career going

"When I looked back at my videos I couldn't believe how well I'd done. My family is very proud of me," he says.

"My goal is to get back into work - and this has raised my confidence even more."

The experience has given Carla a fresh belief in herself too.

"I've learnt not to underestimate myself - and that was a big one for me as I do tend to underestimate what I'm capable of.

"Maybe I need to look at myself a bit more and be aware of just how much I can do.

"I might have to take things slower than other people - but I can still do it."

Kerry Anthony says the workshops helped the group to build resilience and confidence

Inspire chief executive Kerry Anthony says the project is something very different to what the charity would normally do.

Much of its work involves helping people who are dealing with mental ill-health, homelessness or addiction - but Kerry says that talking about those "heavy" topics through humour has been "wonderful" for those in the stand-up workshops.

"People who use our services... have worked with us over the years to use their voice around very serious issues to do with mental ill-health.

"This was a time that they could use their voice in a totally different way.

"Comedy isn't a treatment for mental ill health - but comedy is important for everybody."

Abaserukira Reta Zunze Ubumwe za Amerika mu biganiro hagati ya Ukraine n'Uburusiya bashikirije iciyumviro c'uko Ukraine yokura ingabo zayo zisigaye mu karere ka Donbas, hanyuma na yo ikemererwa kwinjira mu runani OTAN/NATO, nk'uko Perezida Volodymyr Zelensky yabivuze.

Amerika ntiremeza ayo majambo ya Zelensky, ariko umwe mu bategetsi bayo yabwiye BBC ati "ivyiyumviro bitandukanye biracari mu biganiro, ariko amasezerano ya nyuma ategerezwa kwemerwa n'impande zompi".

Zelensky yavuze aya majambo inyuma y'uko intumwa za Amerika zihuye na Perezida Vladimir Putin w'Uburusiya hamwe na Zelensky mu twigoro twa Amerika two guhagarika intambara hagati y'Uburusiya na Ukraine.

Kyiv (ubutegetsi bwa Ukraine) imaze igihe kirekire yipfuza kwinjira muri OTAN, ariko ico ciyumviro carigeze kuba kirwanywa na Amerika n'ibindi bihugu. Uburusiya na bwo nyene bumaze igihe buvuga ko budashobora kwemera uwundi munywanyi wa OTAN ku rubibe rwabwo.

Muri Ruhuhuma (2) 2022, Uburusiya bwatanguje intambara yeruye kuri Ukraine ubu bukaba bugenzura igice kinini ca Donbas, akarere kazwi cane mu vy'inganda, mu gihe Zelensky na we adahengeshanya kuvuga ko Ukraine itazokwigera irekura ubutaka bwayo.

Mu butumwa bwasohowe n'ibiro vyiwe ku mugoroba w'ejo ku wa gatandatu, Zelensky yavuze ati: "Abanyamerika barabajije bati: 'Bite Ukraine yinjiye muri OTAN? None yova muri Donbas?' Ubu ni bwo bwa mbere iki kibazo gishikirijwe".

Yabandanije avuga ko, hamwe yoronka integuro isobanutse irimwo ivyemezo vy'ubwishingizi bw'umutekano, igisirikare ca Ukraine ntigiterwe igitsure, ikaronswa n'amafaranga yo gusanura igihugu, yobishikiriza abanyagihugu biciye muri kamarampaka.

Ku wa kane, intumwa za Amerika Jared Kushner na Steve Witkoff zagiye i Dublin muri Irlande guhura na Zelensky, inyuma y'umubonano wabo na Putin i Moscou.

Amakuru ya BBC Gahuza ako kanya kuri WhatsApp yawe

Amajambo ya Putin hamwe n'ay'abategetsi ba Kremlin (ibiro vy'umukuru w'igihugu c'Uburusiya) yerekana ko Uburusiya butigeze buhindura aho buhagaze kuri iyo ntambara. Kugira ngo habe amasezerano y'amahoro, Uburusiya bwasaba ko igisirikare ca Ukraine kigabanywa, ikarekura ubutaka, kandi ikemera kudahengamira ku ruhande urwo ari rwo rwose.

Ukraine yamiriye kure ivyo vyipfuzo vy'Uburusiya, ivuga ko vyotuma igihugu kidashobora kwivuna mu gihe coba gisubiriye guterwa.

Hampande ya Amerika, hari n'ibindi bihugu vya OTAN bifise amakenga ku bijanye no kwemerera Ukraine kwinjira muri uru runani, kandi biranavugwa ko na Ukraine yo nyene ubwayo ibona ko ivyo bitoshoboka muri kino gihe.

Kremlin yo yamye irwanya ico ciyumviro yivuye inyuma, kandi ni imwe mu mvo zatumye Uburusiya butanguza iyi ntambara.

Birashoboka ko intumwa za Amerika zariko ziragerageza kumenya aho Ukraine ihagaze ku kibazo c'ubutaka bwa Donbas buri mu minwe y'Uburusiya. Zelensky aherutse kuvuga ko abahuza b'Abanyamerika babona ko Kyiv itegerezwa kwemera guheba ubutaka kugira ngo haboneke amahoro, kandi ko bayishirako igitsure kugira ngo habe amasezerano vuba bishoboka.

Ukraine yo yemeza ko Uburusiya bufise inyota irengeye kure cane ikibazo ca Donbas, kandi imaze igihe ibona ko OTAN ari yo nyishu yonyene y'umutekano wayo.

Rero birashoboka ko Zelensky yashize ahabona ico ciyumviro kugira ngo yongere yugurure ikiyago casa n'icugawe kera.

Avuga ko ico kibazo ubu "cagarutse mu biyago" mu rwego rw'ibiganiro bikomeye cane ku mutekano w'Uburaya.

Bisa n'uko ayo majambo ya Zelensky ari uburyo bwo guhangana n'inyifato y'Uburusiya bwasubiye kudadaza. Moscou (ubutegesti bw'Uburusiya) ubu iriko isaba "integuro nshasha y'umutekano wa Buraya", ivyo benshi babona ko yipfuza OTAN itagira inguvu.

Iki kibazo gisa n'icari nyamukuru mu biganiro biheruka vyahuje Ukraine, Uburusiya na Amerika i Abu Dhabi muri Emira Zunze Ubumwe z'Abarabu muri ino ndwi.

Haciye amasaha makeyi Zelensky avuze ayo majambo, Jared Kushner yagerageje kwerekana ko ata co Amerika yemereye Ukraine ku bijanye no kwinjira muri OTAN, asaba ko ivyerekeye ivyo biganiro biguma "mw'ibanga" kuko ari ikibazo gisaba ubwitonzi bwinshi.

Mu majambo yasa n'ayanegura Kyiv, Kushner yavuze ko hari "ibiganiro bikorwa mu mpisho" bigamije kurondera ibindi vyiyumviro bishasha vyo guhagarika iyo yise "intambara ibabaje cane".

Uburusiya bugenzura ubu hafi kimwe ca gatanu c'ubutaka bwa Ukraine, harimwo igice kinini c'intara za Donetsk na Luhansk zigize Donbas.

Bwasubiye gushimangira ko budashobora kwemera guhagarika intambara hataraboneka amasezerano ya nyuma y'amahoro arimwo ko Ukraine iheba ibice vya Donbas bitarafatwa n'ingabo z'Uburusiya, hamwe n'akarere ka Crimée/Crimea Uburusiya bwigaruriye ku nguvu mu 2014.

Ivyo biganiro vyabaye mu gihe hari ukutumvikna hagati ya Kyiv na Washington ku bitero vya Ukraine ku nganda z'Uburusiya zitunganya igitoro. Donald Trump yari yasavye Ukraine kubihagarika kugira ngo vyorohereze Uburusiya gutanga mazutu ku masoko mpuzamakungu no kugabanya ibiciro vy'ibitoro.

Mu nyuma Zelensky yagirije bamwe mu bategetsi ba Amerika kugabanya ubushobozi bw'itumatumanako rya internet bwa Starlink Ukraine ikoresha mu bikorwa vyayo vya gisirikare. Ni muri ico gihe nyene Trump na we yavuze ko "igihe kigeze kugira ngo Ukraine igire uwundi mukuru w'igihugu", aca asaba ko haba amatora mashasha.

Amatora ntashoboka muri Ukraine kubera amategeko y'ibihe vy'intambara, ariko Zelensky yari yarigeze kuvuga ko yiteguriye kuyategura mu mezi make inyuma y'amasezerano y'amahoro, kandi ko yova ku butegetsi mu gihe Ukraine yokwemererwa kwinjira muri OTAN.

MN202611_14nwu3iori4.t:
Anthony Gordon joined Barcelona from Newcastle in the summer

Bayern Munich's Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane, Real Madrid's Jude Bellingham, Barcelona's Anthony Gordon - three of England's star players, all of whom are playing their club football abroad.

The Premier League is widely regarded as the most competitive league in the world with the greatest financial muscle, but that does not always translate to the biggest individual profiles and, increasingly, star names are looking elsewhere.

Since Cristiano Ronaldo won the Ballon d'Or in 2008, for example, only Rodri in 2024 was playing in England at the time of being crowned the best player in the world. Michael Owen, in 2001, was the last Englishman to do so while in England.

The trend of English players going abroad has gathered pace since a teenage Jadon Sancho signed for Borussia Dortmund in 2017 and that is reflected in this current Three Lions squad - seven of the initial 25 play outside England.

"Jude Bellingham and Harry Kane were decisive for us in the World Cup and I see no reason they won't be in the future," said England boss Thomas Tuchel when talking about his big stars playing outside of their home country.

"It's good that Anthony has stepped up now. He is the third one. There is obviously a relevance to them playing abroad but I don't see that a player who plays in the Premier League cannot step up and be decisive for us."

At the World Cup in the summer and during the last international break, however, it was those three players' goals and assists that proved decisive.

Currently there are 43 English players on the Football Association's radar playing their club football in Europe.

The FA's technical director John McDermott believes it is a "huge positive" to have so many players playing across Europe.

"I spoke to a couple of the boys that are playing abroad at the moment," he told BBC Sport. "The exposure they get in those leagues, playing Champions League or European football, where you're not necessarily having to bang out 55 games, but you still have got time to do your weight training and your gym work.

"Often if you're playing in the English competition or in the EFL, where it's 46 games - you know it's game, game, game, which is fantastic - but for some players that opportunity to get the training in-between and to practise developing on technique or other areas, there's benefits to that."

McDermott was previously at Tottenham Hotspur and says that even when he was in club football, he was a "big believer" in players going abroad to "develop character" and "independence".

"I think being in another changing room and learning another language just puts you under the pressure to adapt," he added.

"And I think for any young person that ability not only to become technically, tactically more adept, but also culturally have to pick up something else - it's huge and prevents people from becoming complacent or just getting used to the same old, same old."

Gordon said in the recent international break he feels he gets more respect now he plays for one of Europe's elite sides, compared with when he was at Newcastle.

"I think he's always been respected," McDermott said.

"I remember when Trips (Kieran Trippier) came back, and Trips was a good player, but when he came back from Atletico (Madrid) I noticed he was just maybe tighter technically and noticed there was a change that Kieran came back with.

"So I'm not sure if he's respected more ... but I think you want all of the players - whether they stay in England [or not] - every six months you see this sort of incremental step where they've added something, another dimension to the game.

"That can sometimes come in this country, obviously, playing with different players, being in new competitions, but I think going abroad definitely helps that.

"And I've seen that with Anthony already and some of the other boys. They come back, it's four months since you've seen them and there's another dimension there."

McDermott is keen to make clear that developing in England can still be of a huge benefit and that Jarell Quansah and Jobe Bellingham, two of England's squad who are now playing in Germany, also played in the EFL.

"There's all different ways, I don't think there's this elixir, I don't think there's this magic formula, 'this is the way'," McDermott said.

England reached the semi-finals of the World Cup for just the third time in their history in the summer.

McDermott was asked if he thought now the Three Lions had more players abroad, it could help develop England's style or performance in major tournaments.

"Yeah, possibly. Again don't underestimate if you're playing now in the Champions League at an English club," he said.

"We would like more players in the pipeline. I think at the moment we're on about 26% or 27% English-qualified players playing the Premier League.

"We've got 40 to 50 players playing at Champions League quality and playing in European football, top Premier League clubs, so let's not underestimate our own product."

McDermott says it is clear the impact having players in different countries is having on the squad, but it is then down to the manager to blend the style.

"I think the different cultural experiences they get, the different exposure they get to play in different types of football is fantastic.

"But still, the England manager has got to try and find that singular blend when they come back of the English players, the Spanish players, the German players, the Italian players, it's all sort of an eclectic mix that they're bringing."

England's record goalscorer, appearance maker and captain Harry Kane is playing his club football in Germany with Bayern Munich, while Jude Bellingham has never played in the Premier League - leaving Birmingham for Borussia Dortmund and now Real Madrid

Gordon has impressed since making his move to Barcelona in the summer with three goals and five assists in 15 appearances in all competitions.

The 25-year-old is regularly lining up with some of the best players in the world, in a front line alongside Lamine Yamal and Raphinha.

The lure of European giants like Real Madrid, Barcelona and Bayern Munich is hard for any player to turn down.

Arsenal's approach for Vinicius Jr this summer was always going to be hard to complete as the famous white shirt and lifestyle in Madrid is, for most players, the pinnacle.

But does moving abroad to one of Europe's top clubs also alter people's perceptions of English players?

"I always felt in England, people respected me because I was fast and I pressed, but they never actually respected the quality and IQ that I play with," Gordon said in a recent interview with ITV.

"Only the players I play with ever seem to notice that. I think now I'm at Barcelona and I play a different style, those qualities are highlighted much more and people are actually starting to take notice that I'm not just quick."

Gordon produced some standout moments in the World Cup, assisting both of Kane's goals in the last-32 win over DR Congo, winning a penalty in England's last-16 win over Mexico and scoring the goal to put England ahead in the semi-final against Argentina.

Captain Kane said the winger is "showing that he belongs at the highest level, for Barcelona and England" and that Gordon is "relishing" being one of England's "main men".

"I think it's great," added England and Leeds striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin. "The fact that we've got top-level English players playing abroad now at top European clubs, I think it's only good for English football and us as a national team.

"You see they bring different experiences that they're learning from overseas and they bring it into this group and I think as you can see they're only growing in confidence and as players and I think it's only a positive thing."

President Paul Kagame has joined other Heads of State and Government in Phnom Penh, Cambodia, for the opening session of the 20th Summit of the International Organisation of La Francophonie (OIF).

The opening ceremony featured addresses by several leaders, including French President Emmanuel Macron and OIF Secretary-General Louise Mushikiwabo, who officially ushered in the high-level discussions.

The summit brings together leaders and representatives of Francophone countries to discuss shared priorities, strengthen cooperation and address political, economic, social and cultural challenges facing the French-speaking world.

Rwanda’s participation reflects its continued engagement in the Francophonie platform and its commitment to strengthening international partnerships and cooperation.

The 20th Francophonie Summit is taking place in Phnom Penh from November 14 to 16, 2026, bringing together leaders to deliberate on the future of the organisation and its role in addressing global challenges.

A federal judge has temporarily blocked the US government's closure of an historic golf course and park in Washington DC.

US District Judge Ana Reyes has been overseeing a months-long challenge to the president's plans for East Potomac Golf Links, which he said would be closed from 15 November for extensive renovations.

Reyes has said Donald Trump cannot close the park nor its golf course, but added that his administration was not required to actively manage either.

Trump, an avid golfer, has said his plans to upgrade the 106-year-old course will create "one of the Best and Most Spectacular Golf Courses anywhere in the World". The BBC has contacted the White House for comment.

Declaring the current course "Trash Island", he announced in October that it would be renovated over 15 months to create a space that "will be open to the Public while, at the same time, designed to the Highest Level of Golf and able to hold World Class Tournaments" - despite the ongoing litigation.

Reyes said in a 30-page decision issued on Saturday that the Trump administration's justifications for the proposed course closures were pretextual and that the government had violated at least two federal laws "to meet an arbitrary deadline".

"The government proposes to close a historic park, daily enjoyed by Washingtonians of all stripes, indefinitely," Reyes wrote.

She said the closure "runs counter to the public interest in utilising national parkland", adding that the government had not "plausibly identified any harm it would suffer from a temporary restraining order that preserves the status quo pending further proceedings".

'Trash Island' or DC landmark? How a golf course got Trump in a messy legal dispute

The legal dispute dates back to February, when the DC Preservation League and others sued over redevelopment plans for the park.

The historic course, which sits two miles (3km) south of the White House, is one of three public courses run by the National Park Service (NPS) in the nation's capital.

The legal fight then escalated in October when the NPS began to cut down hundreds of trees without notifying Reyes until 15 hours before work was set to begin.

After the trees were cut, Reyes ordered the Trump administration to stop tree removal until at least 26 October and give her three business days' notice about making any other permanent changes.

Despite the work stoppage, Trump announced that the course would be closed for 15 months from 15 November to accommodate for the renovations. He also shared a rendering of the course redesign.

"The current Course is old, broken, dilapidated and of no further use or effect. It is in very poor condition, with falling, dangerous and disease-infested trees and, importantly, a collapsing and hazardous seawall," he said in a post on Truth Social.

Reyes has since separately opened an inquiry into whether justice department attorneys had "made misrepresentations to the court and otherwise violated ethical rules".

That included whether giving late notice to the court about the renovation plans had been "done in bad faith", and whether the attorneys failed to correct previously false statements or withheld information.

She said she would carry out the inquiry with a special master, an independent third party.

Watch: People cheer as Pope Leo returns to remote Andes town in former diocese

Pope Leo XIV has spoken about the "suffering of those who are forced to leave their homeland in search of a better future", which he said had left communities under threat, during a visit to an isolated Andean village in his former diocese.

About 6,000 people live in Santa Cruz de Succhabamba, located in a remote part of the Andes mountains of northern Peru, but the Pope's visit still drew a crowd of about 20,000, according to the Vatican.

At an outdoor Mass, the Pope spoke of "declining birth rates that are emptying villages" and the unequal distribution of the land's resources.

More than 40% of the population in the Cajamarca region, where the town is located, live in poverty - the highest figure in Peru, according to official data.

Cajamarca has lost the highest number of people to internal migration, with 729,000 people born there now living elsewhere in Peru.

In his sermon, the Pope thanked those who had made the journey to see him and emphasised the importance of never losing heart, despite life's difficulties.

The pontiff's Latin America tour comes roughly a month after he underwent surgery to remove part of his right lung after a cancerous lump was found during routine checks.

At the start of his trip, he said the care he had received made him think of those who "lack the means to obtain a timely diagnosis" or receive treatment for health conditions.

Santa Cruz is within the Diocese of Chiclayo, where the Pope served as bishop from 2015 to 2023. During his tenure, he visited Santa Cruz several times a year to minister to the town's rural population.

On Saturday, he returned by helicopter and was greeted by singing and cheering. He later did a tour in a popemobile, from which he waved to people who had travelled to see him.

Speaking at a local parish on Saturday, the 71-year-old said he felt "joy" at being able to visit the small town once again.

"It is like a very big dream that the Lord has allowed this servant to come here," he said.

Rev Kevin Noriega, who was ordained in 2018 by the then-bishop, told Reuters the visit had brought "enormous hope and emotion" to Santa Cruz.

He said: "People are eager to experience this Holy Mass ... because after so much time they will be able to see their bishop - 'Father Robert', as they used to call him - now as the Holy Father."

Watch: Why Pope Leo’s visit 'home' to Peru is so significant

Peru is the longest stop on the first tour of Latin America by the leader of the Catholic church, who was elected in May 2025.

The 12-day trip has included stops in Argentina and Uruguay, but his time in Peru carries personal significance.

The US-born Pope not only lived in Peru for long periods between 1985 and 2023 but also became a citizen of the country in 2015, forging close ties with local communities.

The pontiff is set to leave Chiclayo on Sunday, when he will head to Cusco and then on to a Peruvian section of the Amazon rainforest. His tour of the region will conclude on Monday, at which point he will return to Rome.
